purpose: Route the newly surfaced ExoAtom atomic-data publication and the current NIST W II holdings reconciliation into Worldshepherd as a machine-readable cross-validation path without confusing a derived subset with the authoritative full W II transition graph.

source_ingestion_policy.rule: Every substantive unique publication, dataset, advisory, or information item discovered during the inquiry receives a Worldshepherd use or a negative-control role.
source_ingestion_policy.duplicates: Duplicate mirrors, derivative copies, and repeated records are provenance aliases and are not independent evidence.
source_ingestion_policy.search_noise: Search co-occurrence or a numeric collision is not Glob evidence; it receives zero evidence weight unless the underlying physical relationship is independently verified.

sources.title: ExoAtom: a database of atomic spectra in ExoMol format
sources.note: Use ExoAtom as a machine-readable interoperability and parser-validation layer for atomic states/transitions. Its NIST-derived W II subset is useful for reproducible ingestion and cross-checks, but it does not replace the current NIST ASD W II holdings or establish independent physical evidence because it is derived from NIST source material.

sources.title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database W II holdings and levels output
sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.note: Current ASD holdings report 2838 W II lines, all 2838 with level designations, while the levels output reports 264 entries. Preserve this current-authority snapshot as the denominator for coverage and completeness tests.

information_updates.finding: The ExoAtom NIST-derived W II dataset reports 58 states and 71 transitions, whereas current NIST ASD exposes 264 W II level entries and 2838 W II lines with level designations.
information_updates.claims_boundary: The fractions are coverage diagnostics only. ExoAtom is a NIST-derived subset and therefore cannot be counted as independent confirmation of a Glob match or relational motif.

new_capability_plan.purpose: Convert ExoAtom .states/.trans files into lower/upper energy transition rows accepted by the existing Worldshepherd NIST ASD transition-graph analyzer, while retaining source-reported wavenumbers for discrepancy checks.
new_capability_plan.claims_boundary: Adapter output is an interoperability/cross-validation artifact. The authoritative full-graph gate remains the current NIST ASD line export.

next_actions: Implement and test the ExoAtom-to-transition-graph adapter so the NIST-derived W II subset can be replayed through the existing topology analyzer.
Acquire the complete current NIST ASD W II line export and compare full-graph topology against the ExoAtom subset without treating the subset as independent evidence.
Apply multiple-testing or false-discovery correction across all predeclared Glob targets, species, tolerances, and relational motifs before any statistical promotion.
